title: unify-transport-throttle-and-graceful-shutdown-across-sdks-with-version-bumps
author: Ava Moreno
description: Context: Multiple SDKs had divergent transports and shutdown semantics which caused customer-visible flakiness during rolling restarts and when connection pools were under sustained load. Motivation: Provide a single transport contract: backpressure-aware throttling hints, connection pool drain semantics, and a small set of ergonomic helpers so SDK consumers get consistent behavior across Python/TypeScript/Go. This PR implements: 1) A transport-level throttle hint API (Transport.hintBackpressure) that surfaces observed queue depth and tokenized_latency to the retry/queuing layer so retry profiles can modulate pacing. 2) A standardized graceful shutdown sequence: Transport.prepareDrain(), Transport.waitForIdle(timeout), Transport.forceClose(). SDKs now expose a top-level client.closeGraceful(timeoutMs) helper that follows the same flow. 3) Connection pool improvements: per-connection idle pruning tuneables, faster failover when a connection enters transient failed state, and a small concurrency governor so worker threads cannot overcommit batches during spikes. 4) Retry policy adjustments: the retry window now uses a backoff multiplier influenced by transport hints (helps avoid cascading retries when the transport is congested). 5) Cross-SDK parity: Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs use the same low-level contract (same method names and ergonomic surface), with minor language idiomatic differences. 6) Version bumps: python 2.4.0, typescript 1.9.0, go 1.5.2. Compatibility: All changes are opt-in by default; client.closeGraceful is additive and existing client.close() behavior is preserved. For customers who rely on immediate shutdown behavior, nothing changes unless they call the new helper. Migration notes: - To opt into backpressure-aware retries, pass retry_profile = "transport-aware" / { retryPreset: "transport-aware" } / WithRetryProfile("transport-aware") depending on SDK. - If you prefer previous behavior, continue to use existing RetryPreset defaults. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-4301) - [x] Cross-SDK API stubs implemented - [x] Unit & integration tests for drain/timeout semantics - [x] Perf lab runs for connection pooling under load - [x] Docs updated for new client.closeGraceful API Commits summary: - feat(transport): add hintBackpressure contract and connector plumbing - feat(client): expose closeGraceful convenience on top-level clients - fix(pool): reduce idle pruning latency and add soft-concurrency governor - feat(retries): wire transport hint into retry multiplier - chore(ts): bump typescript sdk to 1.9.0 - chore(py): bump python sdk to 2.4.0 - chore(go): bump go sdk to 1.5.2 Files changed (high level): ["sdk-python/redwood/client.py", "sdk-python/redwood/transport.py", "sdk-python/tests/test_graceful_shutdown.py", "sdk-typescript/src/client.ts", "sdk-typescript/src/transport/throttle.ts", "sdk-typescript/test/graceful-shutdown.test.ts", "sdk-go/client/client.go", "sdk-go/transport/transport.go", "docs/sdk-graceful-shutdown.md", "benchmarks/transport-throttle/README.md"] CI notes: initial CI run showed two flaky TS tests (connection-pool timing) which were stabilized by adding a small jitter in the test harness; all checks passed on rerun. Rationale: We observed production incidents where heavy burst traffic + retry storms led to connection saturation and experiments showed that surfacing queue depth to retry heuristics reduced 99p tail and dropped error budgets on a few customer workloads. This change keeps the SDK surface minimal while enabling operators to tune for predictable shutdown and lower tail latency.

review_comments: Diego: Please document the guarantee hierarchy (what signals are best-effort vs guaranteed). Author: Added a paragraph in docs and clarified 'prepareDrain' is best-effort but waitForIdle will observe in-flight requests. Maya: Can the retry integration be toggled at runtime? Author: Exposed a runtime flag via client.options.retryProfile and a small environment variable override for the server-side integration tests. Liam: Are there GC/connection leaks under long-lived clients? Author: Added a pool-prune unit test and a long-running soak test in perf lab; no leaks observed in 48h soak. Several minor nits fixed (ts lint, go vet).
release_notes: Introduce transport.hintBackpressure to surface queue depth and latency to retry heuristics.
Add client.closeGraceful(timeoutMs) to allow deterministic drain on shutdown.
Connection pool tuning: reduced idle prune latency and added soft concurrency governor.
Backwards-compatible: old close() preserved; new behavior is opt-in.
SDK version bumps: python 2.4.0, typescript 1.9.0, go 1.5.2.
